content_text:
The 2026 Nedbank Tour de Great Dyke begins on Thursday bringing together cyclists, mining companies, government officials and community stakeholders for a three-day event celebrating the country’s mineral wealth, tourism and community development.

The tour which runs from 5 to 7 November will start at Zimplats’ Selous Metallurgical Complex with Deputy Minister of Mines and Mining Development Dr Caleb Makwiranzou expected to officiate at the launch.

This year’s edition will also combine sport with intellectual engagement through the launch of The Great Dyke Book: Beyond the Rock on Thursday evening at King Solomon Hotel in Kwekwe.

Written by Minex chairperson Munyaradzi Hwengwere, the book examines the geological, historical, economic, environmental and tourism significance of the Great Dyke one of Zimbabwe’s most important natural resources.

The launch is expected to attract government representatives, mining executives, investors, academics and other stakeholders interested in the mineral-rich geological formation and its contribution to the country’s economy.

Tour director Nobuhle Mahlahla said the event had evolved beyond a sporting competition into a platform for promoting the Great Dyke and supporting disadvantaged communities.

“The Nedbank Tour de Great Dyke has grown beyond a cycling event into a platform for celebrating the Great Dyke and the people, industries and communities that define it.

“We want participants and audiences to appreciate that this geological corridor represents much more than mineral extraction. It is about opportunity and supporting talented but underprivileged children for lasting social impact,” she said.

Mahlahla said the book launch would provide an opportunity to deepen public understanding of the Great Dyke and its economic and historical importance.

“The launch of The Great Dyke Book: Beyond the Rock is one of the major highlights of this year’s tour. It complements the cycling experience by documenting the history, geology, economic significance and wider opportunities of the Great Dyke,” she said.

She added that proceeds from the cycling event and book sales would benefit the Gifted Children Foundation, which supports talented children from disadvantaged backgrounds.

The foundation has so far assisted 157 children, helping them access opportunities to develop their abilities and pursue their ambitions.

“At the heart of this initiative is the belief that we must create opportunities for others. The Gifted Children Foundation gives the tour a meaningful social purpose. We are proud that part of the proceeds will support children whose talents deserve to be nurtured, regardless of their economic circumstances,” Mahlahla said.

Stretching approximately 550 kilometres across Zimbabwe, the Great Dyke contains substantial deposits of platinum group metals, chrome, nickel, gold and other minerals.

It remains a strategic pillar of the country’s mining industry, contributing to employment, foreign currency earnings, investment and economic activity in surrounding communities.

Organisers say the three-day event seeks to promote healthy lifestyles while highlighting the economic, environmental, tourism and social opportunities associated with the geological formation.

Beyond the cycling challenge, the initiative aims to ensure that the benefits generated by Zimbabwe’s mineral wealth translate into meaningful opportunities for communities and future generations.

content_text:
The arts community is mourning the death of theatre actor, director and musician Willing Mhlanga, who died on November 2 following a road accident.

Mhlanga was one of the talented artistes nurtured at Amakhosi Theatre, the renowned arts institution founded by the late cultural icon Cont Mhlanga. He went on to build a successful career in the creative industry as an actor, director and musician.

In addition to his work on stage, Mhlanga was a vocalist who performed and recorded music alongside fellow artistes Zenzo Nyathi, Julian Tshuma and Simon Mhlanga. Together, they formed The Mighty Boys, a band that operated under Amakhosi Theatre.

Fellow Amakhosi Productions artiste Zenzo Nyathi paid an emotional tribute to Mhlanga, describing his shock at the actor’s sudden death.

Nyathi said he had met Mhlanga just weeks before the accident when the late actor visited him to buy paint. During the visit, the two spent hours reminiscing about their theatre days and discussing the possibility of performing together again.

He also recalled seeing Mhlanga along Kami Road in Bulawayo last Friday, when they waved at each other in passing, unaware it would be their final farewell.

In a tribute shared on social media, Nyathi said the news of Mhlanga’s death had come as a heavy blow.

“We spoke for a long time and even joked that one day we should return to the stage and do what we loved most,” said Nyathi.

“Last Friday, I saw you again along Kami Road. We waved at each other, little knowing it would be our last wave while you were still alive.

“Then I received the sad news that you had died in a road accident. It hit me hard. Rest in peace, my brother.”

title: Air Zimbabwe exhibits at WTM London after 14-year absence
summary: Rutendo Nyeve rutendo.nyeve@sundaynews.co.zw AIR Zimbabwe is participating at the World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, marking a return to the premier global…
content_text:
Rutendo Nyeve [email protected]

AIR Zimbabwe is participating at the World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, marking a return to the premier global travel trade exhibition after a 14-year hiatus, as the national carrier seeks to rebuild its international profile following the resumption of direct flights to the United Kingdom.

The event is a leading business-to-business gathering for the global travel and tourism industry, and is being held at ExCeL London from 3 to 5 November 2026 .

WTM London annually brings together travel professionals, destination marketers, airlines, tour operators, and travel agents from around the world, with recent editions attracting participants from more than 180 countries and territories.

The airline’s return to WTM comes months after it restored its Harare–London service in July 2026, ending a 14-year suspension of the route .

The service operates three times weekly between Robert Gabriel Mugabe International Airport and London Gatwick South Terminal, providing the only nonstop connection between Zimbabwe and the UK .

The flights are currently operated under a wet-lease arrangement with Spain’s Plus Ultra Líneas Aéreas, an arrangement that allows Air Zimbabwe to resume the route despite regulatory restrictions on its own aircraft in UK airspace .

In a statement, Air Zimbabwe said its participation in WTM London is strategically significant as the carrier seeks to re-establish visibility and raise awareness among international travel industry stakeholders.

“The airline’s return to WTM London after a 14-year hiatus is strategically significant as it seeks to re-establish its visibility, raise awareness among international travel industry stakeholders, and position its direct service as a convenient travel option for passengers between Zimbabwe and the United Kingdom,” the airline said.

“WTM London brings together travel professionals, destination marketers, airlines, tour operators, travel agents, ground handlers, and other industry players from around the world. The event provides a platform for businesses to develop partnerships, explore new markets, and identify opportunities within the global tourism value chain.”

The participation is particularly important given the broader resuscitation of the airline, which has been rebuilding its operations after years of financial and operational difficulties.

The restoration of the London route has been framed by Government officials as a key component of Zimbabwe’s re-engagement agenda and a catalyst for tourism, trade, and diaspora connectivity .

For Air Zimbabwe, WTM London offers a rare opportunity to engage directly with international buyers and travel trade partners at a time when the carrier is seeking to demonstrate reliability and commercial viability.

The event’s scale, recent editions have recorded tens of thousands of pre-scheduled business meetings and billions of pounds in projected deal value, making it a critical forum for an airline attempting to re-enter the global marketplace .

The airline’s presence at WTM London 2026 will be watched closely by industry observers as a signal of whether Air Zimbabwe can translate restored route access into sustained commercial partnerships and passenger demand.

title: Police warn landlords over renting properties to drug dealers
categories: News; drug awareness campaign; drug dealers; Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP)
summary: Police have warned landlords against renting out rooms and other properties to people who use them to store or consume illegal drugs, saying property owners could face seizure of their homes if they knowingly allow their premises to be used for drug-related activities. Detective Mudzimu, from the Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) Criminal Investigations Department (CID) […]
content_text:
Police have warned landlords against renting out rooms and other properties to people who use them to store or consume illegal drugs, saying property owners could face seizure of their homes if they knowingly allow their premises to be used for drug-related activities.

Detective Mudzimu, from the Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) Criminal Investigations Department (CID) Drug Section, said landlords who continued receiving rent from tenants involved in drug-related activities risked losing their properties under legal provisions introduced in June 2026.

She said some tenants rented rooms without actually living in them, raising questions about the activities taking place inside the properties.

“Usually, what happens is that you will find a person who is looking for a one-room apartment, and the person does not stay there. He only keeps his things inside that room and only comes once a month to collect his or her things and goes. The question is, what will be inside the room that he or she is keeping?” Mudzimu said.

She said the new provisions empowered police to seize properties where landlords knowingly allowed their premises to be used for criminal activities while receiving rental payments.

“Since June 2026, the statutory instrument (SI) has said that if we, as policemen, come to your house and find drugs in your house, and you were receiving rent from the person who was keeping drugs in your house, and you have three months accepting rent from this person, the Government has authorised us to seize your house. The crime is called ‘allowing your premises to be used for criminal use’,” she said.

Mudzimu was speaking on Tuesday at Mzilikazi Baptist Church during a drug awareness campaign organised by the Mzilikazi and Barbourfields Residents Association under the theme, “Arise, Shine and Save the Community”.

She also warned homeowners against allowing people to use backyard structures and sheds for drinking alcohol and consuming illegal substances.

“Those people who have also built a shed behind their house and they allow people to come and drink alcohol and consume illegal substances, if we come more than three times, we are authorised to seize your house. If you allow people to come to your house to consume drugs, we will take your house,” she said.

The detective further warned that everyone found at premises where illegal drugs were being consumed could face arrest, regardless of whether they were personally using the substances.

“If we then also find one or three people who are taking drugs and the rest are not, we are arresting everyone in the premises. Parents must warn their children not to sit with people who smoke cannabis or take crystal meth because if we find him or her sitting with them, even if he or she is not consuming the drugs, we are arresting everyone,” Mudzimu said.

She said people caught possessing or consuming illegal drugs would no longer be dealt with through fines but would instead be taken to court for further assessment and possible prosecution.

“There is no longer a fine for being caught with drugs or the consumption of it. We will take the person to court, and once they are in court, there is an interview that will be going on so that the judge can assess whether the person is fit to be put back into society. If not, he or she will be then taken to prison,” she said.

Meanwhile, Mzilikazi proportional representation councillor Lezina Mohamed said substance abuse was increasingly affecting families and communities, with parents frequently approaching community leaders for assistance after their children became involved in drug use.

She said some parents were reluctant to acknowledge that their children were abusing drugs, making it difficult to intervene and seek appropriate help.

“As community leaders, we always get phone calls from parents saying their child has stolen something or is now mentally ill or he or she is fighting with people. The problem is also on us as parents because we are in denial. We will be knowing our child smokes, but you are in denial,” Mohamed said.

Mohamed said community leaders sometimes advised parents to take affected children to hospital for medical assistance, but some refused, attributing their children’s behaviour to witchcraft.

“There have been many occasions where parents call me as a councillor to come and solve the problem, and I suggest that the child be taken to the hospital, but the parents refuse and say we can’t because the parent believes that he or she has been bewitched by the mother or the uncle or the father or someone in their family,” she said.

She urged parents and residents to acknowledge the scale of substance abuse and work together to address its effects on families and communities.

“We must agree that this problem of drugs and substance abuse is there and it’s affecting society,” Mohamed said.

title: Murder suspect freed on bail after challenging ZRP’s dramatic arrest claims
categories: Crime and Courts; Fatal Stabbing; Knife Attack; Murder; Stabbing
summary: A Bulawayo man accused of fatally stabbing his friend and evading arrest for nearly four months has been granted US$300 bail by the High Court. Leonardo Beechey appeared before Justice Naison Chivhayo on Monday facing a murder charge in connection with the death of Tafadzwa Zephania Gorokotah in February. According to the National Prosecuting Authority […]
content_text:
A Bulawayo man accused of fatally stabbing his friend and evading arrest for nearly four months has been granted US$300 bail by the High Court.

Leonardo Beechey appeared before Justice Naison Chivhayo on Monday facing a murder charge in connection with the death of Tafadzwa Zephania Gorokotah in February.

According to the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA), Gorokotah’s body was discovered by a passer-by at around 7 am on 6 February along a footpath in Hume Park linking Harare Road and 4th Avenue. He had a deep stab wound to the left side of his chest and a cut on his left hand.

Investigators said a trail of blood stretching about 130 metres towards 1st Avenue and the Bulawayo-Gweru Road was found at the scene. A ZTE Blade A35 mobile phone, a brown wallet and a toothbrush were recovered from the deceased’s pockets.

Prosecutors Constance Mpofu and Elaine Kanengoni opposed Beechey’s bail application, arguing that he was a flight risk, a drug user and that blood-stained clothing had been recovered from him.

Detective Constable Goodwin Samambwa of the CID Homicide department alleged that Beechey had been on the run since February. He said relatives of the deceased had seen Beechey leaving the victim’s residence with Gorokotah on the day of the incident.

Samambwa told the court that police repeatedly searched for Beechey at his home without success before eventually spotting him in a vehicle travelling towards Gweru in late May.

Police allege that Beechey jumped out of the vehicle and tried to flee when he noticed officers. Samambwa said police fired warning shots and chased him on foot before he tripped and was arrested.

However, defence lawyer Takunda Chapisa challenged that account, arguing that it was inconsistent with information contained in the police Request for Remand Form filed at the time of Beechey’s arrest.

Chapisa said the original document made no reference to warning shots or a dramatic foot chase, suggesting the claims were an afterthought by investigators.

He also rejected allegations that Beechey had gone into hiding, arguing that his client had remained at his home throughout the period. To support the claim, the defence submitted an affidavit from Beechey’s mother.

The defence further disputed the State’s allegation that Beechey was with Gorokotah on the day he was killed.

After hearing submissions from both sides, the High Court granted Beechey bail of US$300.

content_text:
In a country often dominated by stories of economic hardship, political divisions and social challenges, Zimbabweans are being challenged to turn the spotlight on themselves by celebrating people who are making a difference in their communities and shaping the country’s future.

The Centre for Innovation and Technology (CITE) has opened nominations for its inaugural CITE Awards 2026, calling on members of the public to identify and recognise individuals whose work, creativity and commitment are contributing to positive change across Zimbabwe.

The awards seek to celebrate people whose contributions often happen away from the national spotlight, from grassroots community builders and young innovators to content creators, diaspora personalities and individuals making an outstanding public contribution.

CITE Director Zenzele Ndebele said the initiative was designed to create a platform where Zimbabweans could recognise achievements and give credit to people whose work deserves wider recognition.

The six award categories are CITE Person of the Year, Community Changemaker of the Year, Young Innovator of the Year, Zim Diaspora Ambassador of the Year, ZPRA Liberation Archives Interviewee of the Year and Content Creator of the Year.

The flagship CITE Person of the Year category will recognise an individual whose work within Zimbabwe has made an outstanding public contribution during the award year. The Community Changemaker of the Year category, meanwhile, focuses on grassroots initiatives and individuals improving lives, solving local problems and expanding opportunities, particularly in underserved communities.

Young people aged between 18 and 35 will compete for the Young Innovator of the Year award, which recognises fresh ideas and practical solutions in technology, business, culture, media and public problem-solving.

The Zim Diaspora Ambassador of the Year category will celebrate Zimbabweans abroad who positively represent the country, while the Content Creator of the Year award recognises creators whose work informs, inspires and engages audiences.

The ZPRA Liberation Archives Interviewee of the Year category will recognise individuals whose testimonies contribute to preserving Zimbabwe’s liberation history. The five eligible interviewees receiving the highest number of nominations will become finalists.

Nominations opened on 2 November and will close on 14 November 2026. Members of the public can nominate themselves or other deserving individuals by completing the online nomination form.

Nominations can be submitted through the official CITE Awards portal:

content_text:
HARARE — Zimbabwe’s equities market closed higher on Tuesday, with gains in financial and mid-cap stocks offsetting losses among several heavyweight counters, while trading activity remained relatively subdued.

The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange All Share Index rose 0.22% to 493.27 points, supported by a 2.41% advance in the Financials Index and a 1.58% gain in the Mid Cap Index. The ZSE Top 10 and Top 15 indices fell 0.13% and 0.07%, respectively, indicating weaker performance among larger listed companies.

Turnover reached ZWG1.46 million from 63 trades, against a total market capitalisation of approximately ZWG113.78 billion. Financial stocks provided the strongest sectoral support, while the agriculture index declined 1.77% and the Consumer Staples Index shed 0.99%. The Materials Index gained 0.54%.

TNCI led the gainers, rising 11.19% to 84.90 cents, followed by WILD, up 7.21% to 5.47 cents, and ZIMR, which advanced 5.54% to 76.25 cents. CBZ gained 4.44% to 2,913.54 cents, while ZBFH added 1.33% to 760 cents.

HIPO was the session’s biggest faller, declining 7.96% to 1,150.31 cents. FML lost 6.02% to 395 cents, while DZL fell 1.96% to 500 cents. Seed Co and TANG shed 1.77% and 1.43%, respectively.

On the Victoria Falls Stock Exchange, the latest available snapshot, dated 2 November, showed turnover of US$1.42 million across 239 trades, with market capitalisation at approximately US$9.10 billion. The VFEX All Share Index slipped 0.15% to 277.93 points.

ZIMW led the reported VFEX gainers, rising 10% to US$0.11, while Padenga advanced 5.04% to US$1.6051. TSL gained 0.73%, with Simbisa and Econet InfraCo recording marginal increases.

Analysts writing for NewZwire have highlighted the importance of assessing Zimbabwe’s equity market through both price performance and underlying liquidity, particularly as investors navigate currency considerations and uneven participation across listed counters. Tuesday’s modest ZSE turnover, alongside divergent index performances, illustrates the selective nature of trading rather than a broad-based market rally.

The session leaves the ZSE All Share Index in positive territory, but the decline in the blue-chip indices suggests that gains remain uneven across the market.

title: Gender groups welcome PSC policy allowing breastfeeding mothers to travel with babies
categories: National; breast feeding mothers; Public Service Commission (PSC)
summary: Gender and women’s rights organisations have welcomed the Public Service Commission’s (PSC) decision to introduce a policy allowing breastfeeding public servants to travel with their babies and a baby minder on approved official trips within Zimbabwe, describing it as a progressive step towards creating family-friendly workplaces. The policy, issued on 23 October 2026, allows eligible […]
content_text:
Gender and women’s rights organisations have welcomed the Public Service Commission’s (PSC) decision to introduce a policy allowing breastfeeding public servants to travel with their babies and a baby minder on approved official trips within Zimbabwe, describing it as a progressive step towards creating family-friendly workplaces.

The policy, issued on 23 October 2026, allows eligible public servants with children aged up to two years to travel with their babies and a minder when undertaking approved official duties.

Under the arrangement, the relevant Ministry will meet the minder’s transport, meals and accommodation costs, subject to established approval procedures and available budgetary provisions.

The minder must be at least 18 years old, while applicants are required to submit a written request accompanied by supporting documentation.

The Zimbabwe Gender Commission (ZGC) commended the PSC for introducing the policy, saying it recognises the challenges breastfeeding mothers face in balancing their professional responsibilities with childcare.

ZGC said the decision promoted gender-responsive and family-friendly workplaces while giving practical effect to constitutional provisions on gender equality and women’s rights.

The commission said the policy was particularly significant in advancing Section 17 of the Constitution, which requires the State to promote gender balance and women’s full participation in all spheres of life; Section 56, which guarantees equality and prohibits discrimination on grounds including sex and gender; and Section 80, which guarantees women equal dignity and opportunities with men in political, economic and social activities.

“The Zimbabwe Gender Commission commends the Public Service Commission (PSC) for introducing a policy allowing breastfeeding public servants to travel with their babies and a baby minder on approved official trips within Zimbabwe,” the Commission said in a statement.

The ZGC said the policy followed its advisory on the matter and welcomed the PSC’s response, describing it as a timely recognition of an urgent gender equality concern affecting women in the public service.

“The Zimbabwe Gender Commission commends the Public Service Commission for its prompt and timely response to the Commission’s advisory on this matter, and for prioritising the issue as an urgent gender equality concern requiring attention, particularly in addressing the challenges faced by breastfeeding mothers in the public service,” it said.

The Commission urged all Ministries, Departments and Agencies to make sure the policy is effectively communicated and implemented so that eligible employees can access its provisions.

It also called for continued reviews of workplace policies to strengthen support for breastfeeding mothers and promote work-life balance.

Another women’s rights organisation, WoMandla, a girls- and women-led organisation based in Zvishavane, also welcomed the development, describing it as a victory for women and caregivers and an important step towards more inclusive workplaces.

The organisation said the policy acknowledged that motherhood and professional responsibilities should not be treated as competing demands.

“For far too long, women have had to navigate the difficult choices between career progression, work responsibilities and caregiving. Policies like this acknowledge the realities of women’s lives and take a practical step towards addressing structural barriers that disproportionately affect women,” WoMandla said.

“We celebrate this development and encourage continued efforts to build workplaces that recognise, accommodate and value care work.”

The organisation argued the policy recognised the often-overlooked contribution of caregivers and the need for institutions to accommodate the realities of women’s lives rather than leave them to manage childcare challenges individually.

“Care is not a personal inconvenience. It is a shared social responsibility. And supporting caregivers is part of advancing gender equality,” the organisation said.

However, WoMandla stressed the announcement should be followed by effective implementation, adequate resourcing and measures to make sure the provisions translate into meaningful support and “reality” for women who need them.

It said the development should also encourage broader efforts to establish workplaces that recognise, accommodate and value care work.

The policy addresses a practical challenge for breastfeeding mothers in the public service, who may otherwise have to make difficult arrangements for childcare when required to travel for official duties.

Such demands can affect their ability to participate fully in work-related activities and professional opportunities.

While the new provision creates an avenue for eligible mothers to travel with their children and a minder, its effectiveness will depend on how consistently government institutions apply the approval procedures and provide the necessary resources.

title: Prosper Found Shot Dead In Cape Town
summary: By A Correspondent | A Zimbabwean national identified as Prosper has been found dead with a gunshot wound to the head … Continue reading "Prosper Found Shot Dead In Cape Town"
content_text:
By A Correspondent | A Zimbabwean national identified as Prosper has been found dead with a gunshot wound to the head in Strand, Cape Town, in another suspected violent killing that has left the Zimbabwean community in South Africa mourning.

Prosper’s body was reportedly discovered near Broadlands, while his seven-seater Honda BR-V was later found in an area known as Masakhanye.

The circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear, including when he was shot, whether he was killed at the scene where his body was discovered and how his vehicle ended up in a different location.

The killing comes amid persistent concerns over gun violence in South Africa, particularly in the Western Cape, where firearms remain a major contributor to murder cases.

South African Police Service (SAPS) statistics show that 1,071 people were murdered in the Western Cape between April and June 2026, with 62% of the killings occurring in the Cape Town metropolitan area. Western Cape Police Commissioner Lieutenant-General Sizakhele Dyantyi has identified firearms as the weapon most commonly used in murder-related cases.

The latest incident adds to concerns among Zimbabweans living in South Africa over the safety of members of their community, following other reported cases of Zimbabwean nationals being shot dead in Cape Town.

news.co.zw

Police investigations are expected to establish the circumstances surrounding Prosper’s death and whether the discovery of his vehicle in Masakhanye is connected to the killing.

May his soul rest in peace.

title: South Africa’s AGOA Exit Threatens 10,000 Jobs and Disrupts US Citrus Trade
summary: CAPE TOWN — South Africa’s planned removal from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) could put between 3,000 and 10,000 jobs at risk while increasing costs across the American citrus supply chain, according to industry and labour representatives cited by Business Insider Africa. The Trump administration intends to terminate South Africa’s eligibility for the […]
content_text:
CAPE TOWN — South Africa’s planned removal from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) could put between 3,000 and 10,000 jobs at risk while increasing costs across the American citrus supply chain, according to industry and labour representatives cited by Business Insider Africa .

The Trump administration intends to terminate South Africa’s eligibility for the US trade programme from 1 January 2027, ending preferential duty-free access for selected exports, including citrus, wine, vehicles and automotive components.

The potential impact is expected to fall most heavily on agriculture and manufacturing, with export-dependent communities in the Western Cape particularly exposed. Although AGOA-related exports account for about 1% of South Africa’s total global exports, the consequences could be significant for businesses whose production and investment decisions have been built around American demand.

The Citrus Growers’ Association of Southern Africa warned that the decision would affect businesses on both sides of the Atlantic. South African fruit entering the US will face ordinary import duties once preferential treatment ends, while mandarins, lemons and grapefruit will also remain subject to a separate 12.5% Section 301 tariff. Oranges are exempt from that additional tariff but will lose their AGOA duty-free status.

The association said South African citrus supports employment in the United States through importing, shipping, handling, distribution and retail. Its exports also complement domestic American production by supplying fruit during periods when local availability is limited.

Redirecting shipments to other markets will not be straightforward. Growers have developed orchards and export arrangements around US demand, while alternative destinations impose different phytosanitary requirements, seasonal conditions and consumer preferences. Competition from countries such as Chile and Peru, which benefit from trade agreements with Washington, could further weaken South African exporters’ position.

South Africa exported approximately US$1.7 billion in goods to the United States under AGOA in 2025, making it the programme’s largest beneficiary. However, several industries were already facing pressure from separate US tariffs, including the automotive, steel and aluminium sectors. Vehicle-export earnings from the American market fell to about R8 billion in 2025, from R17.7 billion a year earlier, according to figures cited by the business sector.

Pretoria has said it will continue engaging Washington while supporting affected exporters and accelerating efforts to diversify trade towards other markets. However, the adjustment could take time, particularly for producers whose infrastructure, supply chains and commercial relationships are closely tied to American buyers.

title: Government steps up Pfumvudza preparations for 2026/27 season
summary: Story by Wellington Makonese MIDLANDS Province is promoting drought-tolerant crops and conservation agriculture as farmers prepare for the 2026/27 summer cropping season amid forecasts of a super El Niño-induced drought. content_text:
Story by Wellington Makonese

MIDLANDS Province is promoting drought-tolerant crops and conservation agriculture as farmers prepare for the 2026/27 summer cropping season amid forecasts of a super El Niño-induced drought.

The approach combines the Pfumvudza/Intwasa programme with agro-ecological tailoring, which encourages farmers to grow crops suited to the rainfall patterns and conditions of their areas.

The provincial launch of the programme was held in Chirape, Gokwe North, where farmers are preparing plots and diversifying into maize, traditional grains and cotton.

Nationally, Government is targeting three million farmers, 16 million Pfumvudza plots and one million hectares for the season.

Agricultural and Rural Development Authority (ARDA) figures show that more than 3.7 million farmers have already prepared over 9.4 million plots.

One farmer said conservation practices, including mulching, were helping them prepare for the season.

“We are grateful for the lessons we are getting here. We are mulching and preparing these plots, and we are confident of beating this El Niño. We are doing maize, small grains, and cotton, all under Pfumvudza,” the farmer said.

Another said access to inputs would improve farmers’ prospects of increasing production.

“With Pfumvudza, there is a chance for us. We are prepared, and with inputs coming, we can get somewhere.”

ARDA Midlands Provincial Director Ms Busiso Olga Mavankeni said farmers in Natural Regions Three, Four and Five were being encouraged to grow sorghum, millet and sunflower because the crops were better suited to the areas’ lower rainfall.

“The farmer has already made 14 plots. These include cotton and traditional grains. In Natural Regions Three, Four and Five, which cover most of the Midlands, we are promoting sorghum, millet and sunflower because they are better suited to these conditions. We are confident that, as a province, we can make a significant contribution towards mitigating the effects of El Niño and achieving our production targets. The presidential program is providing fertiliser, lime and pesticides, while farmers are encouraged to mechanise plot preparation and diversify production.”

The initiative is part of a broader six-pillar National Response Plan, which also covers food reserves, livestock protection, agricultural financing, imports and early-warning systems.

Midlands Provincial Affairs and Devolution Permanent Secretary Dr Edgar Seenza said traditional leaders were helping to mobilise communities to adopt measures that protect livelihoods and conserve available water.

“Traditional leaders have been conscientised and are cascading the same information to headmen, village heads and their communities. We must maximise whatever rainfall we receive, conserve water, protect livestock and safeguard food security. Pfumvudza/Intwasa is central to that effort. I am happy that farmers are preparing.”

Gokwe-Nembudziya legislator Honourable Flora Buka also commended Government for the programme, urging farmers to prioritise crops suited to local conditions.

“We want to thank the President for this programme; our people have already prepared, especially including livestock, so that they get enough water. Villages are being trained; they should value crops that suit our environment,” she said.

title: Government moves to align laws with Constitutional Amendment No. 3
summary: Story by Fairstars Mukungurutse GOVERNMENT is preparing to amend several laws, including the Electoral Act, to align them with Constitutional Amendment Act No. 3 of 2026, enacted in July. Deputy Minister of Justice, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Honourable Nobert Mazungunye said the Ministry would expedite the process of taking the necessary Bills to Parliament. content_text:
Story by Fairstars Mukungurutse

GOVERNMENT is preparing to amend several laws, including the Electoral Act, to align them with Constitutional Amendment Act No. 3 of 2026, enacted in July.

Deputy Minister of Justice, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Honourable Nobert Mazungunye said the Ministry would expedite the process of taking the necessary Bills to Parliament.

He was speaking on the sidelines of a Constitutional Awareness Programme in Mberengwa this Tuesday, where the Ministry was explaining the amendments and promoting public understanding of the Constitution.

“We are here in Mberengwa as the Ministry of Justice on a sensitisation drive, focusing on the Constitution. Following the mantra of the President that we must not leave anyone or any place behind, we are doing just that. We were also unpacking the amendments. The public must know that we now have Amendment No.3 of 2026. At this juncture, there is need for alignment of subsidiary legislation to the Constitution, as amended. As you all know, the Constitution is the supreme law of the land, so any subsidiary legislation should align with the Constitution. For example, the Electoral Act has to be amended to include all the changes. Very soon, as the Ministry of Justice, we will expedite the movement of the Bills into Parliament so that we effect the necessary changes,” he said.

The outreach was welcomed by members of the Mberengwa community, who said the programme had improved their understanding of constitutional rights and responsibilities.

A community leader said the use of local language had made it easier to understand the Constitution and share the information with others.

“This programme is very important to us as community leaders. We are custodians of our communities. Today, the Ministry has explained the constitution in our language, and now we can go and teach our subjects correctly,” the community member said.

Women who attended said they had gained a better understanding of their rights and where to seek help when those rights were violated, while young people and religious leaders also welcomed the initiative.

In a speech read on his behalf, Midlands Minister of State for Provincial Affairs and Devolution Honourable Owen Ncube commended the Ministry for bringing the programme to Mberengwa.

He said constitutional awareness was important in enabling citizens to exercise their rights, fulfil their obligations and participate in national affairs.

The Mberengwa outreach is part of a nationwide programme by the Ministry of Justice, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs to promote constitutional literacy and access to justice.

title: US$72k Cement Fraud Dispute Rages As Respondent Withdraws Opposition
summary: By Crime and Courts Reporter | High Court judge Justice Bongani Ndhlovu is this week expected to determine whether a case … Continue reading "US$72k Cement Fraud Dispute Rages As Respondent Withdraws Opposition"
content_text:
By Crime and Courts Reporter | High Court judge Justice Bongani Ndhlovu is this week expected to determine whether a case in which cement manufacturing giant PPC is accused of withholding a 330-tonne consignment should proceed to trial after one of the respondents last week withdrew an application opposing the reinstatement of the case.

PPC is cited as the first respondent, while its employee, Nicole Botha, is the second respondent in the case brought by complainant Erksales Hardware.

A High Court notice dated October 20 confirms that Botha withdrew her application opposing the reinstatement of the matter, paving the way for Justice Ndhlovu to hear the plaintiff’s application on November 6 after the case was initially removed from the roll.

“Take notice that the second respondent has withdrawn its notice of opposition with each party bearing its own costs,” reads part of the notice.

In case number HCBC835/26, Erksales Hardware alleges that PPC failed to deliver 11 truckloads of cement, each weighing 30 tonnes, despite receiving full payment for the consignment last year.

The 330 tonnes of cement are valued at approximately US$72,600 at current market prices and were allegedly purchased through a PPC sales representative.

However, the consignment was reportedly never delivered, prompting Erksales to approach the court seeking redress. Its initial application was dismissed after Botha opposed it, leading to the subsequent application for reinstatement.

If the matter is reinstated, PPC Zimbabwe and Botha will be required to respond to the allegations, with trial dates to be determined by the High Court.

Mashayamombe and Company represent Erksales, while PPC and Botha are represented by Moyo and Nyoni Legal Practitioners and Calderwood, Bryce Hendry and Partners, respectively.

In July this year, another company, Tri Oceans, took PPC to court over a similar dispute, with the parties eventually agreeing to settle the matter out of court.

title: Minister Mugadza urges churches to protect vulnerable groups
summary: Tendai Gukutikwa Post Reporter CHURCHES should provide safe, supportive and inclusive environments for women, children and people with disabilities, while actively challenging…
content_text:
Tendai Gukutikwa

Post Reporter

CHURCHES should provide safe, supportive and inclusive environments for women, children and people with disabilities, while actively challenging gender-based violence and discrimination, Manicaland Provincial Affairs and Devolution Minister Misheck Mugadza has said.

He said religious institutions had an important responsibility to promote peaceful, respectful and violence-free families and communities through their teachings and engagement with congregants.

Minister Mugadza made the call in a speech read on his behalf by Mutare District Development Coordinator Mr Tendai Kapenzi during the ordination of Bishop Paradza Shava and the admission of Vateveri vaKristu Apostolic Church into the union for the Development of Apostolic Churches in Zimbabwe Africa (UDACIZA) in Marange recently.

“I call upon the church to ensure that vulnerable members of society are protected and treated with dignity, regardless of their circumstances,” he said.

“Ensure that the church becomes a safe and supportive environment for women, children, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable members of society.”

Minister Mugadza said churches should not only preach against violence but also help survivors access the assistance they need, including protection, counselling, healthcare and justice.

“Religious leaders have an important role to play in challenging harmful social norms, promoting mutual respect between women and men, and encouraging peaceful ways of resolving family disputes,” he said.

“No person should be denied safety, dignity or access to assistance on the basis of religious or cultural beliefs.”

He said gender-based violence remained a concern requiring the collective efforts of Government, churches, families and communities, adding that religious teachings should promote love, accountability and respect for human dignity.

The minister said churches were important partners in national development beyond their spiritual responsibilities, as they also provided moral guidance, mobilised communities and promoted peace and unity.

He encouraged religious institutions across Manicaland to complement Government efforts by supporting vulnerable households, promoting responsible citizenship and participating in initiatives aimed at improving community welfare.

“Churches are not only places of worship. They are also centres of moral guidance, community mobilisation, social support and the promotion of peace and unity,” he said.

“I therefore encourage religious institutions to continue contributing to national development by promoting the wellbeing of all people.”

Minister Mugadza said sustainable development required cooperation among Government, churches, traditional leaders, civil society organisations, the private sector and communities.

He also congratulated Bishop Shava on his ordination, describing the appointment as a call to service rather than an opportunity for personal recognition.

He urged the new bishop to lead with humility, integrity, compassion and fairness, while promoting unity among congregants and supporting those facing difficulties.

“Ordination is not merely the attainment of a title or position. It is a call to greater responsibility, servant leadership, humility and commitment to the spiritual and social wellbeing of the people entrusted to your care,” he said.

The minister urged church members to support their bishop and work together in building a congregation guided by unity, participation and mutual respect.

UDACIZA provincial chairperson for Manicaland Reverend Prosper Sithole welcomed Vateveri vaKristu Apostolic Church into the church network, urging other white garment churches to join the organisation.

He said bringing churches together under UDACIZA would create opportunities for cooperation and strengthen their contribution to addressing challenges affecting communities.

“We are happy that Bishop Shava and his church have joined UDACIZA. We encourage more white garment churches to become members so that we can work together, promote responsible church leadership and strengthen our contribution to the welfare of communities,” he said.

Reverend Sithole said churches had an important role to play in promoting the protection of vulnerable people and ensuring that their teachings translated into responsible conduct within congregations and families.

He said cooperation among religious institutions would also help strengthen efforts to promote peaceful coexistence and address social challenges affecting communities.

title: Govt considers expanding private nursing training
summary: The Government is considering expanding private-sector participation in nursing education as part of efforts to increase the number of trained healthcare professionals and meet growing demand for medical services. Speaking at The Avenues Clinic’s 23rd graduation ceremony last week, where 38 specialist nurses graduated in Intensive Care and Operating Theatre Nursing, Health and Child Care […]
content_text:
The Government is considering expanding private-sector participation in nursing education as part of efforts to increase the number of trained healthcare professionals and meet growing demand for medical services.

Speaking at The Avenues Clinic’s 23rd graduation ceremony last week, where 38 specialist nurses graduated in Intensive Care and Operating Theatre Nursing, Health and Child Care Minister Douglas Mombeshora said the move will be guided by the results of an ongoing pilot programme at the Dr Auxillia Mnangagwa School of Nursing in Kadoma.

“The Ministry intends to progressively open up private-sector participation in nurse training beyond the current pilot project being undertaken at the Dr Auxillia Mnangagwa School of Nursing in Kadoma,” said Mombeshora.

He said any expansion will be based on evidence gathered from the pilot programme to ensure the process is properly structured.

“The necessary reviews and evaluations of the pilot will guide us on how and when to expand participation, as well as which institutions and partners are suitably positioned to come on board,” he said.

Mombeshora also praised private healthcare institutions for their contribution to specialist healthcare, nursing education, infrastructure development and investment, singling out The Avenues Clinic for its longstanding role in training specialist nurses.

He said that since introducing Intensive Care Nursing in 1978 and Operating Theatre Nursing in 1979, the clinic has trained 347 specialist nurses in the two fields.

The minister further welcomed the clinic’s introduction of Oncology and Palliative Care Nursing programmes and its partnership with the University of Zimbabwe, which provides clinical attachment opportunities for students.

title: Stop Madness: President Chamisa Blasts Mnangagwa Regime Over Heartless Demolitions
summary: Tinashe Sambiri| Citizens leader President Nelson Chamisa has condemned the ongoing demolitions targeting citizens’ structures and businesses, accusing the Mnangagwa … Continue reading "Stop Madness: President Chamisa Blasts Mnangagwa Regime Over Heartless Demolitions"
content_text:
Tinashe Sambiri| Citizens leader President Nelson Chamisa has condemned the ongoing demolitions targeting citizens’ structures and businesses, accusing the Mnangagwa regime of destroying livelihoods and inflicting suffering on hardworking Zimbabweans.

In a strongly worded statement on Monday, Chamisa described the demolitions as cruel and inhumane, questioning why people who had invested their life savings into establishing businesses and building structures were now being subjected to destruction.

“THE UNELECTABLE ARE HEARTLESS… This is cruel, heartless and deeply inhumane. No government should subject its own citizens to such treatment,” Chamisa said.

He argued that affected citizens had invested their money, time and resources into building structures and establishing legitimate sources of income, only for authorities to move in and destroy their investments.

“You allow innocent, hardworking citizens to invest their life savings, time and resources into building structures and establishing honest livelihoods. Then, at this late stage, you descend upon them with demolitions, destroying their investments, livelihoods and hopes for the future,” he said.

Chamisa maintained that the affected people should not be treated as criminals simply because they were attempting to earn an honest living.

“These are people trying to eke out an honest living, not criminals. Their dignity, rights and livelihoods must be respected and protected,” he added.

The Citizens leader said responsible leadership should prioritise the protection of citizens and their economic interests rather than preside over the destruction of livelihoods painstakingly built over the years.

He called for an immediate end to the demolitions and what he described as the persecution of ordinary citizens.

“Stop this madness. Stop the violations. Stop the persecution. Responsible leaders must protect citizens, not destroy them and decimate livelihoods citizens worked so hard to build,” Chamisa said.

content_text:
The City of Bulawayo has postponed the implementation of Operation Hlanzeka, which targets informal traders and illegal structures, following calls for further engagement with affected businesses.

The operation, which was scheduled to begin on Sunday, November 1, has been suspended with immediate effect and is expected to resume in two weeks.

In a public notice issued on Tuesday, Town Clerk Christopher Dube said the postponement would allow the local authority to engage stakeholders before proceeding with the operation.

“The City of Bulawayo as a listening local authority is facilitating further engagement of all concerned stakeholders,” the notice said.

The postponement also gives informal traders operating in undesignated areas more time to relocate their businesses to approved trading sites, remove illegal structures and move their goods.

The operation targets micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) operating from undesignated locations, including road servitudes, parking bays and pavements.

The council said it recognised the contribution of small businesses to livelihoods but maintained that trading from unauthorised spaces would not be permitted.

“The City of Bulawayo would like to emphasise that, while it values the role played by MSMEs in supporting livelihoods, trading from undesignated places such as road servitudes, parking bays and pavements is not allowed,” the notice said.

The local authority urged affected businesses to use the postponement period to comply with municipal by-laws and move their operations to designated trading areas.

“We urge all affected MSMEs to co-operate with the authorities during this transition period to ensure a smooth relocation process,” the notice said.

The postponement follows concerns over the impact of enforcement measures on informal traders, many of whom depend on street trading for their livelihoods.

The council said affected traders could seek clarification and assistance from its Town Planning Department’s MSMEs section at the 9th Tower Block Offices.

title: Zimbabwe vulnerable to drone warfare, warns defence minister
categories: General; Drone; Drone Attack; Drone Warfare; Drones
summary: Zimbabwe is vulnerable to modern drone warfare and is losing its best pilots to foreign recruiters due to poor salaries, Defence Minister Oppah Muchinguri-Kashiri has warned. Speaking at the pre-budget seminar in Bulawayo on Friday, Muchinguri-Kashiri cited the Russia-Ukraine war, where she said 70 per cent of casualties are caused by drones used for surveillance, […]
content_text:
Zimbabwe is vulnerable to modern drone warfare and is losing its best pilots to foreign recruiters due to poor salaries, Defence Minister Oppah Muchinguri-Kashiri has warned.

Speaking at the pre-budget seminar in Bulawayo on Friday, Muchinguri-Kashiri cited the Russia-Ukraine war, where she said 70 per cent of casualties are caused by drones used for surveillance, precision strikes and psychological warfare.

“The new warfare: a $10,000 drone destroys $200 million worth of military equipment,” she said.

She said it is not just countries using drones, but terrorists are also using them for drug trafficking and smuggling gold and minerals.

“If we do not have equipment to bring down these drones, we are heading towards disaster. We are vulnerable,” she said.

Muchinguri-Kashiri said Zimbabwe is still thinking about helicopters and fighter jets while warfare has become cheaper and deadlier with artificial intelligence, facial recognition and micro-killer drones.

“A small drone can come into this room and just kill one person; somewhere in South Africa, somewhere in Nigeria, can send a drone just to destroy and kill one person,” she said.

The minister said the Air Force of Zimbabwe has lost almost 50 per cent of its pilots to greener pastures. She said it costs over US$40,000 to train one pilot, but salaries are poor.

“Everyone comes to Zimbabwe to recruit. We need to protect them by paying them very well,” she said.

Muchinguri-Kashiri said there are no funds for Zimbabwe Defence Forces modernisation. ICT equipment received only ZiG15 million against a ZiG34 million bid, which is 43 per cent, while only ZiG125 million was allocated for building maintenance against a need of ZiG1.6 billion, which is 6 per cent.

title: Tongaat MD calls for collaboration as sugarcane yields drop
summary: INCREASE GUMBOMIRROR REPORTER CHIREDZI –Tongaat Hulett Zimbabwe (THZ) Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Tendai Masawi has called for collaboration, co-ordination and partnerships among players in the sugar industry in order to identify constrains, develop practical solutions and increase yields.Masawi said this on the sidelines of the 31st Zimbabwe Sugarcane Industry Seminar (ZSIS) held at […]
content_text:
INCREASE GUMBO MIRROR REPORTER

CHIREDZI –Tongaat Hulett Zimbabwe (THZ) Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Tendai Masawi has called for collaboration, co-ordination and partnerships among players in the sugar industry in order to identify constrains, develop practical solutions and increase yields. Masawi said this on the sidelines of the 31st Zimbabwe Sugarcane Industry Seminar (ZSIS) held at Hippo Valley Country Club from Thursday to Friday this week. The seminar, hosted by the Zimbabwe Sugar Association (ZSA), and attended by 501 farmers sought to explore ways of increasing sugarcane production particularly for outgrowers at a time when yields are going down. Outgrowers currently harvest 71t of sugarcane per hectare compared to the top production figure of 120 tonnes per hectare. “The sugar industry is a strategic national industry with shared responsibility among farmers, millers, refiners and marketers. Good collaboration increases productivity, and we need to close the gap between the miller-cum-planter and farmers,” said Masawi. He urged farmers to work with other stakeholders to identify constraints affecting sugarcane production and develop practical solutions to improve yields. Masawi said stronger partnerships across the industry are essential in addressing production bottlenecks and ensuring that farmers and other players worked towards a common goal of improving productivity. Key stakeholders for collaboration are farmers, millers, refiners and marketers ZSA director, Audrey Mabveni said small-scale sugarcane farmers, also known as outgrowers increasingly recognise the importance of working together to improve performance. “There is a lot of cohesiveness among outgrowers. They are realising that they have to work together, which is this year’s theme,” said Mabveni. A top member of the sugarcane growers board, Bernadette Chipembere said the seminar had highlighted the potential of collaboration in addressing declining yields among outgrowers. “What is affecting us as outgrowers is the drop in yields, and if we are going to come together as stakeholders and look at yields and production, I think things will get better,” said Chipembere.

title: Spanish Footballer Jesús de Miguel Dies After Horror On-Pitch Collision With Goalkeeper
categories: Local Zimbabwe News; sport; World News
summary: Spanish Footballer Jesús de Miguel Dies After Horror On-Pitch Collision With Goalkeeper Spanish football has been plunged into mourning following the death of CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel, who succumbed to injuries sustained in a collision during a league match on Monday. The 30-year-old was rushed to hospital after a clash with FC Andorra […]
content_text:
Spanish Footballer Jesús de Miguel Dies After Horror On-Pitch Collision With Goalkeeper

Spanish football has been plunged into mourning following the death of CD Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel, who succumbed to injuries sustained in a collision during a league match on Monday.

The 30-year-old was rushed to hospital after a clash with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono in the closing moments of their Segunda División encounter. Although he was initially reported to be in a stable condition, his health deteriorated overnight.

Tenerife confirmed his death on Tuesday, prompting emotional tributes from his club, former teammates and football teams across Spain and beyond.

Also Read: Diogo Jota Dies In Fiery Car Crash Just Days After Wedding – What We Know

Collision Brings Match to a Halt

The incident happened near the halfway line as De Miguel chased the ball towards the end of the match.

Owono had moved well outside his goal to clear the ball when he collided with the Tenerife forward at speed. The goalkeeper was immediately shown a red card for the challenge.

After realising the seriousness of the situation, Owono returned to check on De Miguel, who had remained motionless on the pitch.

Medical personnel attended to the striker, and players from both teams appeared visibly distressed as he received treatment. The match was subsequently abandoned with only minutes remaining.

Condition Deteriorates Overnight

De Miguel was taken directly to hospital, where initial reports indicated that he was stable despite the severity of his injuries.

However, Tenerife later revealed that his neurological condition had deteriorated overnight before confirming that he had died on Tuesday morning.

The club expressed its devastation in a statement, saying there were no words to ease the pain of losing the player.

“ Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true,” Tenerife said.

The club added that it stood with De Miguel’s family, friends and supporters as they struggled to come to terms with the loss.

Tributes have also come from football teams across Spain and other parts of the world.

title: Mnangagwa’s US$2.6 Billion Mirage Crashes As ZIDA Hype Produces Only 1,945 Jobs
summary: Tinashe Sambiri| President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s government has been exposed for selling Zimbabweans yet another investment fantasy, after parading US$2.61 billion … Continue reading "Mnangagwa’s US$2.6 Billion Mirage Crashes As ZIDA Hype Produces Only 1,945 Jobs"
content_text:
Tinashe Sambiri| President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s government has been exposed for selling Zimbabweans yet another investment fantasy, after parading US$2.61 billion in licences that translated into a paltry 1,945 jobs.

In a post on Monday, Zanu PF Murakashi Mairosi Watungwa wrote that “According to the Zimbabwe Investment and Development Agency’s Q3 2026 report, 182 new licences were issued with a projected value of US$2.61 billion, a 64.1% jump from Q2 despite a similar licence count.”

He claimed that “Foreign currency cash injections more than doubled to US$1.49 billion, with manufacturing overtaking mining as the lead sector at US$1.22 billion against US$1.06 billion, while the Midlands emerged as the top destination, attracting US$1.41 billion.”

But the figures collapse under scrutiny. Despite Mnangagwa’s constant claims of Zimbabwe being open for business, the quarter produced almost no employment.

“The true test, however, lies in conversion and jobs. Only 1,945 jobs were recorded from monitored projects in the quarter, 1616 in mining, 287 in manufacturing and 42 elsewhere, underscoring the urgent need to broaden employment beyond mining,” Watungwa conceded.

The admission confirms that Mnangagwa’s US$2.61 billion is only on paper, with the bulk of jobs still trapped in exploitative mining while manufacturing remains dead.

The report also exposes how the regime has been inflating investment numbers since 2022.

“Crucially, the report distinguishes between projected value declared at licensing, US$295.5 million in promotion-linked commitments, and US$1.95 billion in verified on-the-ground inflows, which covers only about 22% of projects licensed since 2022 and should not be measured against the cumulative US$63.63 billion projected since then,” he wrote.

It means Mnangagwa’s much-touted US$63.63 billion investment pipeline is a lie, with only 22% ever verified on the ground.

Investor confidence is also collapsing under Mnangagwa’s watch.

“With commitments as a share of qualified leads falling to 11.4% from 23.5%, enquiries down 23.6%, and fewer than three in ten renewals completed on time, ZIDA’s stated Q4 focus on investor follow-up, aftercare and renewals will determine how much of the US$2.61 billion ultimately materialises.”

With enquiries down, commitments halved and investors failing to renew licences, the US$2.61 billion is nothing but propaganda to prop up Mnangagwa’s failed “#ZimEconomyRising” and “#Vision2030AReality” slogans.
